v.rationale: All three pass their suites and share the same overall shape: enum casts, afterCommit dispatch, a global RateLimited 5/s limiter, retryUntil plus MaxExceptions, failed() recording the reason, and guards on shipment_reference and shipment_notified_at. impl-3 ranks first: it is the simplest. It treats a 422 as a recorded business outcome, not a failed job, honours Retry-After on 429, sends an Idempotency-Key, claims the email atomically, and has the most modern tests (withFakeQueueInteractions, fakeSequence). Its weakness is a non-atomic double-dispatch guard with no overlap lock, softened by the idempotency key. impl-1 is second: it has the strongest markAsPaid (atomic conditional update that refuses cancelled orders) and an overlap lock, and its tests run through the real queue middleware. But it has a confirmed NULL-comparison bug in failed() and no idempotency protection against the 'hangs then retries' duplicate-shipment case. impl-2 is third despite the most defensive middleware: re-calling markAsPaid on a shipped order regresses shipment_status to pending (confirmed). It treats all non-429 4xx (for example a 401 from a bad token) as permanent failures, ignores Retry-After, and sends the email before recording it.
